rationale: Low-to-medium complexity. No code is produced in this task — output is a technology decision document. Key risks: (1) technology choices that appear compatible but have hidden offline/local-first limitations discovered late, (2) scope creep by including advanced charting in design artifacts, (3) dependency version conflicts not caught at research stage. Mitigation: structured trade-off documentation per requirement axis, explicit scope exclusion checklist, and compatibility matrix verification before sign-off. Estimated effort: 1 research cycle + 1 review cycle.

Complexity: MEDIUM. Risk: LOW-MEDIUM. Primary risks are (1) SQLite vs DuckDB contested decision requiring benchmark evidence, (2) Pydantic v2 breaking changes vs v1 ecosystem compatibility, (3) transitive dependency conflicts between FastAPI/Pydantic/Alembic. No implementation risk at this phase — pure research and documentation. All libraries are well-established OSS with permissive licenses (MIT/Apache-2.0 expected). Human intervention checkpoint required before T-002 begins per acceptance criteria gate.

Complexity: LOW-MEDIUM. Risk: HIGH-IMPACT if done poorly (all downstream phases depend on this). No implementation code involved.
